findings.title: No API Interface — Direct Database Access Only
findings.description: The application is a VB6 desktop fat-client that connects directly to a Microsoft Access .mdb file via Jet OLEDB. There is no REST, GraphQL, AsyncAPI, or any programmatic API interface. Integration requires direct database access or UI automation.
findings.gap: No API surface exists. The only integration path is direct database manipulation or UI automation — both brittle, unauditable, and unsuitable for agent consumption.
findings.recommendation: Build a REST API layer wrapping core CRM operations to provide a stable, documented integration surface for agents.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application has no authentication mechanism. It connects to the database using a hardcoded password and identifies users only via Environ('USERNAME') — a Windows session variable, not machine identity authentication.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication exists. No OAuth, API key, mTLS, or service account mechanism. Cannot distinguish which agent made a call.
findings.recommendation: Deploy a centralized identity provider (Amazon Cognito with app client credentials) requiring all clients to authenticate before data access.

findings.title: Credentials Hardcoded in Source Code
findings.description: Database credentials are hardcoded directly in source code (DB_PW = 'crm2005pw'). ODBC connection string with credentials embedded in the compiled EXE. No secrets management system is used.
findings.gap: No secrets management (Secrets Manager, Vault, or equivalent). Credentials permanently exposed in version control and compiled binary.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials. Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation for all database credentials.

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application exposes no documented API interface. It uses ColdFusion file-based routing (index.cfm, download.cfm) with HTML responses rendered server-side. There is no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface — integration would require UI automation or direct database access.
findings.gap: No programmatic API surface exists. The only interface is an HTML web page designed for human browser interaction.
findings.recommendation: Create a REST API layer with JSON responses for document listing and download operations.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses ColdFusion session-based authentication only. No support for service accounts, API keys, OAuth2 client credentials, mTLS, or any machine identity mechanism. Agent authentication is impossible without human-style session login.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists. Only interactive session-based auth is available.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication for machine callers.

findings.title: No Input Validation — SQL Injection Vulnerable
findings.description: The application performs zero input validation. url.q is passed directly into SQL via string concatenation. url.id is used directly in SQL without type checking. Both create SQL injection vulnerabilities. No structured error responses exist for malformed input.
findings.gap: Complete absence of input validation. No parameterized queries. Active SQL injection vulnerabilities.
findings.recommendation: Replace all string-concatenated SQL with parameterized queries (<cfqueryparam>). Add input type validation for url.id (must be numeric). Implement structured error responses.

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application serves HTML via Django views with raw SQL. No REST API, no JSON endpoints, no API documentation exist. Integration requires HTML scraping or direct database access.
findings.gap: No API interface exists for agent consumption. Only HTML responses via Django templates and raw string concatenation.
findings.recommendation: Build a REST API with JSON responses using Django REST Framework. Requires migration from Python 2.7/Django 1.4 to a supported stack first.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: Only Django session-based authentication exists. No OAuth2 client credentials flow, no API key authentication, no mTLS configuration, no service accounts.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism. Agents cannot authenticate without using human session credentials.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key or OAuth2 client credentials authentication with per-agent principal attribution.

findings.title: Credentials Hardcoded in Source Control
findings.description: Django SECRET_KEY and database password are hardcoded in plaintext in settings.py committed to the repository. No secrets management system exists.
findings.gap: All credentials in plaintext in VCS. No secrets management, no rotation, no encryption at rest for credentials.
findings.recommendation: Remove secrets from settings.py. Move to environment variables immediately, then migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation.

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application exposes a single HTTP endpoint at /loan via Struts 1.3 action mapping, returning server-rendered JSP pages. No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Integration requires UI automation or direct database access.
findings.gap: No programmatic API interface suitable for agent consumption. Only server-rendered HTML via Struts form submission.
findings.recommendation: Expose loan calculation and submission as a REST API with JSON payloads (e.g., POST /api/loans).

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: Container-managed authentication via request.getRemoteUser() only. No support for service account, machine identity, client credentials OAuth 2.0, API key with principal attribution, or mTLS.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism. Designed exclusively for human browser users.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key or OAuth2 client credentials authentication for the new API surface with principal attribution.

findings.title: Hardcoded Credentials in Source Code
findings.description: Database credentials hardcoded directly in Java source code as static final constants: DB_URL, DB_USER (loan_app), and DB_PASS (loanApp2010). Committed to source control.
findings.gap: No secrets management. Credentials in source code visible to anyone with repository access.
findings.recommendation: Move credentials to AWS Secrets Manager with rotation. Remove hardcoded values and rotate exposed credentials immediately.

findings.title: No modern API interface — SOAP-only with deprecated RPC/encoded style
findings.description: The application exposes a SOAP 1.1 RPC/encoded endpoint via JAX-WS. The WSDL is hand-maintained and drifts from implementation. No REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface exists. Agent tool frameworks cannot bind to SOAP services without significant custom adapter logic.
findings.gap: No REST or modern API interface for agent tool binding. SOAP with RPC/encoded style is incompatible with agent frameworks.
findings.recommendation: Create a REST facade (e.g., Spring Boot REST controller or API Gateway with SOAP-to-REST transformation) that wraps the existing SOAP operation as a POST /orders endpoint with JSON request/response.

findings.title: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists
findings.description: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists in the codebase. WS-Security mentioned in README but not implemented in visible code. No OAuth2 client credentials flows, no API key authentication, no mTLS, no service account definitions, no API Gateway authorizers.
findings.gap: No foundation for authorization, audit, or identity suspension. Every downstream security control is invalidated.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an API Gateway with OAuth2 client credentials authorizer. Issue per-partner client_id/client_secret pairs with principal attribution in access tokens.

findings.title: Database credentials hardcoded in source code
findings.description: Database credentials are hardcoded directly in source code: DB_USER = 'partner_app' and DB_PASS = 'partner2009'. These credentials are committed to version control. No secrets management system is used.
findings.gap: Critical security vulnerability. Credentials not rotatable without code changes. Exposed in git history.
findings.recommendation: Move credentials to AWS Secrets Manager with automatic rotation enabled. Replace hardcoded values with Secrets Manager SDK calls.

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The system exposes no documented REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. Integration requires batch file exchange via plaintext FTP and JCL job submission on z/OS. There are no HTTP endpoints, no RPC interfaces, and no programmatic integration points accessible to an agent.
findings.gap: No API exists. The only integration mechanism is FTP of fixed-width files and direct mainframe job submission via JCL/CA-7 scheduling.
findings.recommendation: Build a REST API layer wrapping payroll operations (trigger run, query status, retrieve results) with OpenAPI documentation.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The system has no machine identity authentication mechanism. The only credential is a hardcoded FTP username/password (payroll/PayR0ll2003!) in the JCL file. There is no OAuth2, no API key authentication, no mTLS, no service account model, and no principal attribution.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication exists. The single hardcoded FTP credential cannot distinguish callers, cannot be scoped, and cannot be attributed in audit logs.
findings.recommendation: Implement service account authentication with unique identities per caller. Replace FTP with SFTP using key-based authentication with distinct keys per integration partner.

findings.title: No Structured API — HTML-Only CGI Response
findings.description: The application exposes an HTTP CGI endpoint at /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi accepting query parameters sku and qty. The response format is text/html — raw HTML markup, not a structured machine-readable format. No API documentation exists. An agent would need to parse HTML output to extract pricing data.
findings.gap: No structured (JSON/XML) API response format. HTML output requires scraping for programmatic integration. No API documentation.
findings.recommendation: Add a JSON response mode triggered by an Accept: application/json header or format=json query parameter. Document the endpoint contract in an OpenAPI specification.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: Zero authentication mechanism exists at any layer. Any network-reachable client can call /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi without presenting credentials. No OAuth2, no API keys, no mTLS, no JWT verification, no API Gateway authorizer.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. No principal attribution for audit. Cannot distinguish which agent or caller made a request.
findings.recommendation: Deploy an API Gateway in front of the service that requires API key or OAuth2 client credentials before forwarding requests.

findings.title: Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses a single static API key ('ship-2013-abc123-static') hardcoded in server.js. All callers share the same key with no principal attribution. No OAuth2, mTLS, Cognito, or machine identity mechanism exists.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication. A single shared static key provides no caller attribution, no rotation capability, and no per-agent identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement API Gateway with IAM authorization or Cognito app client credentials flow. Each agent/caller gets a unique client ID logged with every request.

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application exposes Rails controller actions (index, create, show) but has no documented API interface. No REST documentation, no OpenAPI spec, no route definitions. Controller renders HTML views only. Integration would require UI automation or direct database access.
findings.gap: No documented, stable API interface exists. Agents cannot bind to an undocumented HTML-rendering controller.
findings.recommendation: Create a RESTful JSON API layer and publish an OpenAPI 3.x specification.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application has no authentication mechanism. The controller notes 'No before_filter auth on some actions (legacy oversight).' No OAuth2, no API key authentication, no mTLS, no service accounts. All requests are anonymous.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication exists. All requests are anonymous and unattributable.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication with principal attribution.

findings.title: Credentials Committed to Source Control
findings.description: Payment gateway credentials (merchant_id, api_password) are committed to source control in plaintext in config/payment.yml. The controller loads these directly from the checked-in file. No secrets management system exists.
findings.gap: Credentials are hardcoded in version-controlled files. No secrets management or rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Remove config/payment.yml from version control, rotate credentials immediately, store in AWS Secrets Manager.

findings.title: No Documented API Interface
findings.description: The application is an ASP.NET WebForms UI with no REST, GraphQL, or AsyncAPI interface. Integration would require direct database access or UI automation (RPA). There are no API endpoints — only server-rendered .aspx pages with postback-driven interactions.
findings.gap: No programmatic API exists. The only integration path is direct SQL or UI automation.
findings.recommendation: Extract data access logic into a service layer and expose as a REST API (e.g., ASP.NET Web API or modern framework).

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses ASP.NET Forms Authentication with session cookies. There is no support for service accounts, OAuth2 client credentials, API keys, or mTLS. The only authentication mechanism is human-interactive browser-based login.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists. An agent cannot authenticate without simulating a browser login flow.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 client credentials or API key authentication for programmatic access with principal attribution.

findings.title: Plaintext Credentials in Configuration
findings.description: Database credentials are stored in plaintext in web.config (User ID=ts_app;Password=Time2006!). No secrets management system exists. No rotation mechanism. The README confirms this is a known issue.
findings.gap: Credentials hardcoded in configuration committed to version control. No rotation. A source code leak would expose the database password.
findings.recommendation: Migrate credentials to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Remove plaintext credentials from web.config.

findings.title: No Machine Identity Authentication
findings.description: The application uses PHP session-based authentication exclusively. No OAuth2 client credentials flow, no API key mechanism with principal attribution, no mTLS, and no service account support for machine callers. Agents cannot authenticate programmatically.
findings.gap: No machine identity authentication mechanism exists. An agent cannot authenticate without simulating a browser session.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key authentication with per-agent principal attribution as an alternative auth path for /api/* endpoints.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions — Single Shared Credential
findings.description: Single shared database password grants full read-write access to all data. No role differentiation, no IAM policies, no mechanism to scope permissions per caller.
findings.gap: No authorization model. All callers have identical full read-write access. Cannot create scoped, least-privilege permissions for agent identities.
findings.recommendation: Implement RBAC in the new API layer with separate roles for read-only agents vs write-enabled agents.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. Single database connection permits all SQL operations without per-action permission checks. No RBAC, no ABAC.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict agents to read-only operations. All connected clients have full DML access.
findings.recommendation: Implement fine-grained RBAC with action-level checks (canRead, canWrite, canDelete per resource type) in the new API layer.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation or Delegation
findings.description: No identity propagation exists. Environ('USERNAME') is a local environment variable, not a propagated identity token. No JWT, no OAuth token exchange, no on-behalf-of flows.
findings.gap: No identity propagation mechanism. Cannot distinguish agent-as-self from agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 on-behalf-of flows in the new service architecture with separate IAM roles for different actor types.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. The CreatedBy field stores a mutable Windows username in the database — not an immutable audit log. No CloudTrail, no immutable storage, no log file validation.
findings.gap: No immutable audit trail. Cannot prove compliance or conduct forensics on agent actions.
findings.recommendation: Deploy CloudTrail with log file validation and S3 Object Lock for immutable audit storage.

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension Mechanism
findings.description: No identity management system. Single shared password. Cannot suspend or revoke individual agent identities without changing the shared password affecting all users.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate or suspend a misbehaving agent without disrupting all other users.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent identity lifecycle management with independent revocation capability as part of identity provider deployment.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Unscoped — All Fields Accessible
findings.description: System stores customer PII (names, creator usernames). No API response scoping (no API exists — direct database access returns all fields). No access control differentiation. No formal classification metadata.
findings.gap: B1: All fields accessible to any connected client (no API filtering). B2: No access control differentiation (single shared credential). B3: No classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Implement field-level response filtering in the new API layer to exclude PII from agent-facing endpoints unless explicitly scoped.

findings.title: Data Residency Requirements Undocumented
findings.description: Data resides on on-premises Windows file server (S:\CRM\sales.mdb). No documented residency requirements, no compliance frameworks referenced. Cloud migration may trigger regulatory obligations.
findings.gap: No documented residency constraints. Data movement to cloud or LLM providers may create compliance violations.
findings.recommendation: Conduct data residency assessment. Document regulatory constraints. Ensure target AWS region meets requirements before migration.

findings.title: No Input Validation — SQL Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: No input validation. User input concatenated directly into SQL strings. SQL injection vulnerability confirmed. No parameterized queries, no validation library, no type checking.
findings.gap: Zero input validation at any boundary. SQL injection possible. No structured validation error responses.
findings.recommendation: Replace string-concatenated SQL with parameterized queries immediately. Add request validation middleware in the new API layer.

findings.title: Incomplete Temporal Metadata and No Freshness Signaling
findings.description: CreatedOn via Now() exists but with no timezone normalization (VB6 Now() returns local time). No UpdatedAt field. No freshness signaling. Nightly sync means 24h data staleness with no machine-readable indicator.
findings.gap: Incomplete temporal metadata. No timezone normalization. No freshness signaling for cached or eventually-consistent data.
findings.recommendation: Store all timestamps in UTC. Add updated_at fields. Include Cache-Control and X-Data-Freshness headers in API responses.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema documentation, versioning, or contract testing. Database schema only discoverable by reading inline SQL in source code. No migration files, no changelog, no breaking change detection.
findings.gap: No documented or versioned schema. No breaking change detection for agent tool bindings.
findings.recommendation: Create formal schema definition and implement versioned migrations. Use OpenAPI spec with schema validation in CI for the new API.

findings.title: No Test Coverage
findings.description: No automated tests exist. README confirms 'No tests, no build server.' Zero test coverage. No test files, no test framework, no CI pipeline.
findings.gap: No test coverage. Cannot verify agent-facing API behavior.
findings.recommendation: Build comprehensive API test suites (contract tests, integration tests) running in CI for the new service.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: Data stored in unencrypted Microsoft Access .mdb on SMB file share. Database 'password' is access control, not encryption. No KMS, no disk-level encryption.
findings.gap: No encryption at rest. Sensitive customer data in plaintext on network share.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to AWS managed database (RDS, DynamoDB) with KMS customer-managed encryption keys.

findings.title: No Sandbox or Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment. No build server. Deployment is manual EXE copy. No separate environment configurations, no seed data scripts.
findings.gap: No staging environment for testing agent behavior safely against realistic data.
findings.recommendation: Create containerized local development environment with synthetic seed data.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback Capability
findings.description: No compensation or rollback mechanism. Write operations are single INSERT statements with On Error Resume Next error swallowing. No transaction management, no saga pattern, no undo capability.
findings.gap: No rollback capability. Failed multi-step operations leave data in partial state. Cannot undo agent-initiated writes.
findings.recommendation: Implement transaction management and compensating actions in the new service layer. Use saga patterns for multi-step workflows.

findings.title: No Queryable State Interface
findings.description: No API-accessible queryable state. State only accessible via direct database queries. No GET endpoints, no status APIs for agents to inspect state before acting.
findings.gap: No queryable state interface for agents. State locked behind direct database access.
findings.recommendation: Design comprehensive GET/query endpoints in the new API layer enabling agents to inspect state before acting.

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or any machine-readable specification exists.
findings.gap: No machine-readable spec for agent tool generation.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI specification once a REST API surface exists.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No error handling exists. No structured error codes or machine-readable error bodies. Errors surface as raw ColdFusion runtime exceptions.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON error responses with error code, message, and retryable indicator.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: Binary authorization model — users are either authenticated (session exists) or not. No role-based access, no resource-level permissions, no mechanism to grant differentiated access to different callers.
findings.gap: No scoped permissions mechanism. All authenticated users have identical access.
findings.recommendation: Implement role-based access control with at minimum read-only and admin roles.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. Once authenticated, any user can list all documents and download any file. No distinction between read/write/delete permissions.
findings.gap: No fine-grained authorization. Cannot restrict an agent to specific actions.
findings.recommendation: Implement action-level authorization checks (canRead, canDownload per document category).

findings.title: No Identity Propagation
findings.description: Flat session model. No JWT forwarding, no token exchange, no on-behalf-of flows. Cannot distinguish agent-as-self vs agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.gap: No identity propagation mechanism. No delegation flow.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2/JWT-based identity propagation with on-behalf-of support.

findings.title: No Credential Management
findings.description: Credentials stored in CF Administrator UI. Password 'cfadmin' disclosed in README. No secrets management, no rotation.
findings.gap: No secrets management system. Hardcoded weak credentials. No rotation.
findings.recommendation: Migrate to AWS Secrets Manager with automated rotation. Remove credentials from documentation.

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging of any kind. No CloudTrail, no application logs, no immutable log storage. No record of who accessed what.
findings.gap: Complete absence of audit trail.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging with principal attribution for every operation.

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension Mechanism
findings.description: No mechanism to suspend individual agent identities. Session-only auth provides no per-identity revocation capability.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without affecting all users.
findings.recommendation: Implement API key authentication with per-key revocation capability.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: Data resides on local disk and SQL Server on a single EC2 instance. No residency controls documented. No controls preventing cross-jurisdiction data movement.
findings.gap: No data residency documentation or technical controls.
findings.recommendation: Document residency requirements. Implement network egress controls.

findings.title: No PII Redaction Infrastructure
findings.description: No PII redaction mechanisms exist. Database stores user identifiers (uploaded_by, session.fullname). No log scrubbing or masking libraries.
findings.gap: No PII redaction. If logging is added, PII would leak without explicit controls.
findings.recommendation: Implement PII redaction from the start when adding logging infrastructure.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema documentation, no versioning, no contract testing, no breaking change detection. Database schema only inferrable from SQL in .cfm files.
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings would break silently on schema changes.
findings.recommendation: Document the schema and implement API versioning with contract tests.

findings.title: No Infrastructure Governance
findings.description: No IaC. Infrastructure is manually configured. No peer review, no drift detection. Single Windows EC2 instance.
findings.gap: No infrastructure governance. All changes are manual and untracked.
findings.recommendation: Define infrastructure in Terraform/CloudFormation with PR review and drift detection.

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. Deployment is manual file copy over network share. No automated testing or contract verification.
findings.gap: No automated testing or contract verification before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Establish CI/CD pipeline with automated testing and API contract tests.

findings.title: No Rollback Capability
findings.description: No rollback mechanism. Manual file copy deployment with no versioning, no blue/green, no canary.
findings.gap: No automated rollback capability.
findings.recommendation: Implement versioned deployment with automated rollback triggers.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing, no structured logging, no correlation IDs. Zero observability instrumentation.
findings.gap: Cannot trace or debug agent-initiated requests.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON logging with correlation IDs and distributed tracing.

findings.title: No Alerting on Error Rates or Latency
findings.description: No alerting infrastructure. No CloudWatch alarms, no health checks, no monitoring integration.
findings.gap: System degradation is invisible to agents and operators.
findings.recommendation: Implement health check endpoints and CloudWatch alarms for error rates and response latency.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, no WAF, no application-level throttling. Application is directly exposed on IIS.
findings.gap: Runaway agent loops could overwhelm the application and database.
findings.recommendation: Implement rate limiting via API Gateway or reverse proxy with throttling rules.

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or Smithy model exists. No auto-generated specs. Searched for openapi.*, swagger.*, *.graphql, *.smithy — zero results.
findings.gap: No machine-readable API specification for agent tool generation.
findings.recommendation: Generate OpenAPI spec from REST API using drf-spectacular when API is built.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Errors return Django HTML tracebacks (DEBUG=True). No structured JSON error format, no error codes, no retry guidance.
findings.gap: No machine-readable error responses. Agents cannot distinguish retriable vs terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement JSON error responses with error code, message, and retryable boolean. Disable DEBUG mode.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: Django basic auth model with no scoped permissions. Views perform no permission checks — any authenticated user can access any ticket.
findings.gap: No mechanism to scope agent access to specific resources or actions. All authenticated users have identical access.
findings.recommendation: Implement role-based access control with granular permissions and resource-level scoping.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. Views have no permission decorators or checks. Any caller reaching the view can perform any supported action.
findings.gap: Cannot enforce read-only vs write access at the action level.
findings.recommendation: Add permission classes with action-level enforcement (e.g., DjangoModelPermissions).

findings.title: No Identity Propagation or Delegation
findings.description: No JWT parsing, no OAuth2 token exchange, no on-behalf-of flows. Session-only auth with no mechanism to propagate or delegate identity.
findings.gap: Cannot distinguish agent-as-self vs agent-on-behalf-of-user. No token-based identity propagation.
findings.recommendation: Implement JWT-based authentication with delegation claims when building REST API.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No audit logging exists. No CloudTrail, no application-level audit log, no request logging middleware. Only a debug print statement.
findings.gap: Zero audit trail. Cannot determine who accessed or modified any ticket.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured audit logging with principal attribution and immutable storage (CloudWatch Logs with Object Lock).

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension Mechanism
findings.description: No mechanism to suspend or revoke individual agent identities. Only Django session auth exists — no API keys, no service accounts, no OAuth clients to revoke.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without affecting all users.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent API keys or OAuth2 client credentials with individual revocation capability.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Unscoped in API Responses
findings.description: System stores user-specific data (requester, ticket subjects). Views return all fields with no filtering or response scoping. No access differentiation.
findings.gap: Agent-facing responses include all stored fields with no scoping. No access differentiation. No classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Implement serializers that exclude sensitive fields from agent-facing responses. Add OAuth scopes for access differentiation.

findings.title: PII Logged Without Redaction
findings.description: User search queries printed to stdout via print statement with no redaction. User input could contain PII (names, emails, account numbers).
findings.gap: User input logged without PII redaction. No log scrubbing infrastructure.
findings.recommendation: Remove debug print statement immediately. Implement structured logging with field allowlists.

findings.title: No Input Validation or Schema Enforcement
findings.description: Zero input validation. Parameters passed directly into raw SQL via string formatting. SQL injection vulnerability present. No type checking or sanitization.
findings.gap: No input validation at API boundary. Malformed or malicious input accepted without rejection.
findings.recommendation: Implement request validation and parameterized queries. Return structured 400 responses with field-level error details.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema documentation, no API versioning, no contract testing, no breaking change detection. No JSON Schema, no migration files, no version URLs.
findings.gap: No versioned API contracts. Agent tool bindings would break silently on changes.
findings.recommendation: Adopt OpenAPI-first design with versioning and contract tests when building API.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: Zero IaC. Manual deployment via git pull + Apache restart. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or Ansible. No peer review or drift detection.
findings.gap: No IaC governance. Infrastructure manually managed with no change tracking.
findings.recommendation: Define infrastructure as code (Terraform or CDK). Require PR review. Enable AWS Config for drift detection.

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild. Deployment is manual. No automated tests or contract validation.
findings.gap: No automated testing or contract validation. API-breaking changes undetectable before production.
findings.recommendation: Set up CI/CD pipeline with automated tests and API contract validation.

findings.title: No Rollback Capability
findings.description: No automated rollback. Only git revert + manual Apache restart. No blue/green, no CodeDeploy, no feature flags.
findings.gap: No automated rollback mechanism. Recovery requires manual intervention.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated deployment with rollback triggers (CodeDeploy or blue/green via ALB).

findings.title: No Sandbox or Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox, staging, or test environment. Single EC2 instance with production deployment only. No Docker Compose for local testing, no seed data.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior before production.
findings.recommendation: Create Docker Compose-based local development environment with seed data for agent testing.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No OpenTelemetry, no X-Ray, no trace ID propagation, no JSON logs, no correlation IDs. Only a print statement for debugging.
findings.gap: Cannot trace or correlate agent-initiated requests through the system.
findings.recommendation: Implement OpenTelemetry with structured JSON logging and correlation IDs.

findings.title: No Alerting on Error Rates or Latency
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration. Bare EC2 instance with no monitoring infrastructure.
findings.gap: System degradation undetectable until users report it.
findings.recommendation: Deploy CloudWatch alarms for HTTP error rates and response latency.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting or Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, no WAF, no application-level rate limiting middleware. Apache mod_wsgi with no throttling.
findings.gap: Application fully exposed to traffic storms from runaway agent loops.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway or WAF with per-caller rate limits. Add application-level throttling.

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or equivalent machine-readable specification exists in the repository. The only API definition is the Struts action mapping in struts-config.xml.
findings.gap: No machine-readable API specification. Agent tool definitions require entirely manual authoring.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI 3.0 specification for the loan API surface alongside REST API implementation.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: No structured error handling. All methods throw Exception without catching or formatting. Errors surface as generic HTTP 500 from WebLogic container.
findings.gap: No structured error responses, no error codes, no machine-readable error bodies, no retryable/terminal distinction.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON error responses with error code, message, and retryable indicator.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: No authorization model beyond container-managed authentication. All authenticated users have identical full access to all operations.
findings.gap: No scoped permissions model. No mechanism to differentiate access levels per caller.
findings.recommendation: Implement RBAC with at minimum read-only and write roles, enforceable per caller identity.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: Cannot enforce action-level authorization. Single endpoint handles both read (calculate) and write (submit) operations differentiated only by form field value with no permission checks.
findings.gap: No action-level authorization. Read and write operations not separable by permission.
findings.recommendation: Separate calculate and submit into distinct endpoints with independent authorization checks.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation
findings.description: No identity propagation support. Uses request.getRemoteUser() without delegation, token exchange, or JWT parsing. Cannot distinguish agent-as-self vs agent-on-behalf-of-user.
findings.gap: No on-behalf-of flows, no token exchange, no agent/human distinction.
findings.recommendation: Implement OAuth2 token exchange or JWT propagation with actor/subject distinction.

findings.title: No Audit Logging
findings.description: No logging of any kind. No logging framework imported. No audit trail, no immutable log storage, no CloudTrail integration.
findings.gap: Zero audit logging capability. Cannot trace or audit actions after the fact.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured audit logging for all operations with immutable storage (CloudTrail + S3 Object Lock).

findings.title: No Agent Identity Suspension
findings.description: No mechanism to suspend or revoke individual agent identities. Container-managed WebLogic realm has no per-identity disable without affecting all users.
findings.gap: No per-identity revocation capability. Cannot isolate misbehaving agent.
findings.recommendation: Implement per-agent API keys with revocation capability or deploy behind API Gateway with usage plans.

findings.title: Sensitive Data Unscoped in API Responses
findings.description: Application stores PII (applicant names) and financial data (principal, rates). Struts form beans expose all fields without filtering. No response scoping, no field exclusion, no access control differentiation.
findings.gap: B1: No API response scoping for sensitive fields. B2: No access control differentiation. B3: No formal classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Implement response filtering to exclude PII fields from agent-consumable responses. Add access control differentiation.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: Financial/PII data stored in Oracle with no residency controls, no GDPR/LGPD compliance references, no region-specific configurations. No controls to prevent cross-region transmission to LLM providers.
findings.gap: No data residency controls or documentation for financial/PII data.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements and implement controls to prevent cross-region transmission to LLM providers.

findings.title: No Selective Query Support
findings.description: No query capabilities — no pagination, filtering, or sorting. No GET endpoints that return data sets. Only form submissions returning JSP pages.
findings.gap: No pagination, filtering, or sorting. No query API exists.
findings.recommendation: Implement query endpoints with pagination (limit/offset or cursor-based), filtering, and sorting.

findings.title: No Input Validation — SQL Injection Vulnerability
findings.description: No input validation at the API boundary. Applicant name concatenated directly into SQL string — SQL injection vulnerability. No validation framework, no type checking beyond Java casting.
findings.gap: No input validation, no schema enforcement. Critical SQL injection vulnerability.
findings.recommendation: Fix SQL injection immediately by using parameterized queries. Implement comprehensive input validation with structured error responses.

findings.title: No PII Redaction Controls
findings.description: No logging framework present and no PII redaction controls exist. When logging is implemented, PII (applicant names) will leak without preventive controls.
findings.gap: No PII redaction infrastructure. No log scrubbing, no masking libraries.
findings.recommendation: Implement PII masking from day one when adding logging. Use field-level masking for applicant names.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning, no API contracts, no breaking change detection. No CI pipeline. No versioning mechanism of any kind.
findings.gap: No schema documentation, no versioning, no breaking change detection.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning and schema documentation from the start of REST API implementation.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code
findings.description: No IaC. Manual WAR deployment via WebLogic admin console. No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or Kubernetes manifests. No peer review of infrastructure changes, no drift detection.
findings.gap: No infrastructure governance. Entirely manual infrastructure management.
findings.recommendation: Define infrastructure as code (Terraform or CDK) as part of modernization. Implement PR-based review and drift detection.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No tracing (no X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry), no structured logging (no JSON logs), no correlation IDs, no trace ID propagation. Zero observability.
findings.gap: No tracing or structured logging capability. Agent-initiated requests are completely opaque.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured JSON logging with correlation IDs and X-Ray or OpenTelemetry tracing.

findings.title: No Alerting on Error Rates or Latency
findings.description: No alerting configured for error rates or latency. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no monitoring infrastructure.
findings.gap: No monitoring or alerting. Cannot detect target system degradation.
findings.recommendation: Implement CloudWatch alarms for error rates and latency at the API layer.

findings.title: No Queryable Current State
findings.description: No GET endpoint or query API to inspect current state. Application only supports form submission. No way to query existing loan applications or check status.
findings.gap: No queryable state endpoint. No GET API for reading records.
findings.recommendation: Implement read endpoints (GET /api/loans, GET /api/loans/{id}) alongside the write API.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, no WAF, no application-level rate limiting middleware. A runaway agent loop could overwhelm the application and Oracle database.
findings.gap: No rate limiting at any layer. No protection against agent traffic storms.
findings.recommendation: Deploy behind API Gateway with usage plans and throttling, or add application-level rate limiting middleware.

findings.title: Machine-readable spec (WSDL) is unreliable and deprecated
findings.description: WSDL exists but is hand-maintained, acknowledged to drift from implementation, and uses deprecated RPC/encoded style. No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, or Smithy model exists.
findings.gap: No reliable machine-readable spec for agent tool generation.
findings.recommendation: Create OpenAPI 3.x specification for the REST facade once created.

findings.title: Unstructured error responses — raw exception messages
findings.description: Errors returned as unstructured strings: 'ERROR:' + e.getMessage(). No error codes, no retryable indicators, no consistent format.
findings.gap: Agent cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Replace catch-all with structured error responses including code, message, and retryable boolean.

findings.title: No authorization model — all callers have identical access
findings.description: No authorization model exists. The SOAP endpoint has a single operation with no mechanism to differentiate caller permissions. All callers have identical full write capability.
findings.gap: Cannot scope an agent identity to specific permissions. All callers inherit the same broad surface.
findings.recommendation: Implement scoped authorization at API Gateway layer with OAuth scopes (orders:read, orders:write).

findings.title: No action-level authorization — only write operations exist
findings.description: Single write operation only. No read operations available. No action-level authorization exists — cannot enforce read-but-not-write within the same resource type.
findings.gap: Cannot allow an agent to read order records without granting write capability.
findings.recommendation: Add read operations (GET /orders/{id}) and implement method-level authorization.

findings.title: No audit logging — zero observability of operations
findings.description: No logging of any kind exists. No logging imports, no logging framework, no CloudTrail configuration. The authenticated principal is not logged because authentication does not exist.
findings.gap: No audit trail for any operation. Cannot determine who submitted an order.
findings.recommendation: Add structured logging that records caller identity, operation, timestamp, and outcome. Store in immutable destination.

findings.title: No identity management — cannot suspend agent access
findings.description: No identity management exists. Without machine identity authentication, there is no mechanism to suspend or revoke an individual agent's access.
findings.gap: Cannot isolate a misbehaving agent without blocking all traffic.
findings.recommendation: After resolving AUTH-Q1, implement per-agent API keys or OAuth client IDs that can be individually revoked.

findings.title: No data residency documentation or controls
findings.description: Oracle database at hardcoded internal IP with no documented residency requirements. No GDPR/LGPD compliance references. No region-specific storage configuration.
findings.gap: Cannot determine whether cross-region data transmission is permissible.
findings.recommendation: Document data residency requirements for partner order data. Implement network-level controls for approved regions.

findings.title: No PII redaction framework for logging infrastructure
findings.description: No logging exists currently, but no PII redaction framework in place for when logging is added. Raw exception messages may disclose internal details to callers.
findings.gap: No PII redaction infrastructure for future logging implementation.
findings.recommendation: Implement PII redaction from the start when adding logging. Use structured logging with allowlisted fields.

findings.title: No input validation — SQL injection and XXE vulnerabilities
findings.description: No input validation. SQL injection via string concatenation. XXE vulnerability in XML parsing. No size limits, no schema validation.
findings.gap: Malformed or malicious inputs accepted without rejection.
findings.recommendation: Use parameterized queries, validate XML against schema, enforce size limits.

findings.title: No schema versioning or breaking change detection
findings.description: Hand-maintained WSDL drifts from implementation. No versioning, no changelog, no breaking change detection in CI (no CI exists).
findings.gap: Agent tool bindings break silently on changes.
findings.recommendation: Implement API versioning and automated schema comparison in CI.

findings.title: No Infrastructure as Code — manually provisioned
findings.description: No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, Helm, or Kustomize. Service runs on manually provisioned JBoss AS 5.1 on RHEL 6.
findings.gap: Integration surface not defined as code, not peer-reviewed, not drift-monitored.
findings.recommendation: Define infrastructure as code using CloudFormation or Terraform.

findings.title: No CI/CD pipeline — manual Ant builds
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Build performed manually via Ant. No automated testing.
findings.gap: Cannot catch API-breaking changes before production.
findings.recommendation: Create CI/CD pipeline with automated build, tests, and schema comparison.

findings.title: No automated deployment or rollback capability
findings.description: No automated deployment. WAR deployed manually on JBoss with no rollback automation.
findings.gap: Cannot roll back if a change breaks agent-facing APIs.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated deployment with rollback (CodeDeploy, ECS blue/green).

findings.title: No sandbox or staging environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment. No Docker Compose, no environment-specific configurations, no seed data scripts. Single production deployment.
findings.gap: No safe environment to test agent behavior before production.
findings.recommendation: Create containerized local development environment with seed data for agent testing.

findings.title: Zero observability — no tracing, no structured logging
findings.description: No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, trace ID propagation, structured logs, or correlation IDs. Zero observability instrumentation.
findings.gap: Agent-initiated request failures are completely undiagnosable.
findings.recommendation: Add structured JSON logging with correlation IDs and OpenTelemetry/X-Ray tracing.

findings.title: No alerting on error rates or latency
findings.description: No alerting exists. No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no monitoring integration.
findings.gap: Service degradation undetectable proactively.
findings.recommendation: Deploy CloudWatch alarms once observability infrastructure is in place.

findings.title: No compensation or rollback for write operations
findings.description: Single SQL INSERT with no transaction management, no rollback logic, no saga pattern. On failure, raw exception returned but no cleanup occurs.
findings.gap: No compensation or rollback mechanism. Partial state possible on failure.
findings.recommendation: Implement proper database transaction management with rollback on exception. Add compensation endpoints.

findings.title: No rate limiting at any layer
findings.description: No rate limiting exists. No API Gateway, no WAF, no application-level rate limiting middleware. SOAP endpoint directly exposed on JBoss with no throttling.
findings.gap: A runaway agent loop could overwhelm the service and Oracle database at machine speed.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with throttling configuration or add WAF rate rules.

findings.title: Write-only service — no read operations available
findings.description: Only exposes submitOrder write operation. No way to query existing orders, check status, or read current state.
findings.gap: Agent cannot inspect current state before taking action.
findings.recommendation: Add read endpoints (GET /orders, GET /orders/{poNumber}).

findings.title: No Asynchronous Operation Support
findings.description: The payroll batch job runs 5-7 hours with no async patterns — no job submission API, no polling endpoint, no webhook callback, no status query mechanism.
findings.gap: No programmatic async operation support for long-running batch.
findings.recommendation: Implement a job status API with submission, polling, and completion notification capabilities.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions
findings.description: The system has no authorization model. A single hardcoded FTP credential provides unrestricted access to the payroll output files. There are no IAM policies, no role definitions, no permission scoping of any kind.
findings.gap: No mechanism exists to create scoped permissions for different callers. All access uses the same credential with full read/write to the FTP directory.
findings.recommendation: Implement RBAC with per-agent scoped permissions as part of the new API layer.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The system cannot differentiate between read and write access — the FTP credential allows both uploading and downloading files.
findings.gap: No fine-grained RBAC, no ABAC policies, no action-level checks.
findings.recommendation: Build action-level authorization into the new API layer with method-level permissions.

findings.title: No Identity Propagation
findings.description: No identity propagation exists. The system has no concept of caller identity beyond the single shared FTP credential. There is no JWT, no OAuth token exchange, no on-behalf-of flow.
findings.gap: No identity propagation mechanism. The batch job runs under a single z/OS job identity regardless of who initiated it.
findings.recommendation: Implement identity-aware API with token-based authentication that carries caller context through the processing pipeline.

findings.title: Hardcoded Plaintext Credentials
findings.description: Credentials are hardcoded in plaintext directly in the JCL source file: FTP username 'payroll' and password 'PayR0ll2003!'. No secrets management system, no rotation. The credential has been static since at least 2003.
findings.gap: No secrets management. Credentials embedded in source code committed to git. No rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Immediately rotate the exposed credential. Move credentials to AWS Secrets Manager or z/OS RACF credential vault with automated rotation.

findings.title: No Immutable Audit Logging
findings.description: No immutable audit logging exists. JES job output (SYSOUT) captures batch execution but is not immutable, not attributable to a specific caller, and not stored in a tamper-evident manner.
findings.gap: No audit trail identifying who initiated payroll processing or accessed output files. JES spool output is transient and overwritable.
findings.recommendation: Implement immutable audit logging (CloudTrail for AWS components, SMF records retention for z/OS) with principal attribution.

findings.title: No Sensitive Data Access Controls
findings.description: The system stores and processes highly sensitive PII: Social Security Numbers (EMP-SSN) and bank account numbers (EMP-ACCT). There is no access control differentiation — the single FTP credential provides access to all data including SSNs and bank accounts.
findings.gap: B1: No API surface to evaluate response scoping. B2: No access control differentiation — single credential grants access to all sensitive data. B3: No formal classification metadata.
findings.recommendation: Implement tiered access controls separating sensitive from non-sensitive data. SSNs and bank accounts should only be accessible via separately-authorized, audited endpoints.

findings.title: No Data Residency Controls
findings.description: The system processes SSNs (US PII subject to federal and state regulations) and transfers them via plaintext FTP to an EC2 instance. No data residency controls, no encryption in transit.
findings.gap: No data residency documentation. No encryption in transit. Plaintext FTP of regulated PII data.
findings.recommendation: Replace plaintext FTP with SFTP or TLS-encrypted transfer. Document data residency requirements for SSN data.

findings.title: No PII Redaction in Logs
findings.description: No PII redaction controls exist. The FTP step transmits SSNs and bank accounts in plaintext where network logging or FTP server logs could capture them. No log scrubbing or PII masking.
findings.gap: No PII redaction mechanism. No log filtering. Plaintext transmission of PII-containing files creates log exposure risk.
findings.recommendation: Implement PII masking for logging. Replace plaintext FTP with encrypted transfer to eliminate network-level PII exposure.

findings.title: No Selective Query Support
findings.description: The system processes all employee records sequentially with no filtering, pagination, or selective query capability.
findings.gap: No pagination, no filtering, no sorting, no selective retrieval.
findings.recommendation: Implement filtered/paginated query APIs as part of the re-platform.

findings.title: No Input Validation
findings.description: No input validation exists. The COBOL program performs arithmetic on raw input fields without validating data types, ranges, or business rules.
findings.gap: No input validation at any boundary. No schema enforcement. No structured error responses.
findings.recommendation: Add input validation with structured error reporting. Validate SSN format, rate ranges, hours worked bounds.

findings.title: No Temporal Metadata
findings.description: No temporal metadata exists in the data model or output files. No created_at/updated_at fields, no timezone handling, no data freshness indicators.
findings.gap: No timestamps in data records. No freshness signaling.
findings.recommendation: Add temporal metadata (pay period dates, processing timestamp, data effective date) to output records.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning
findings.description: No schema versioning exists. The fixed-width file format (120-byte records) is undocumented beyond COBOL PICTURE clauses. No schema registry, no version numbering, no breaking change detection.
findings.gap: No schema documentation beyond COBOL source. No versioning. No breaking change detection.
findings.recommendation: Document the fixed-width file format as a versioned schema. Implement format version headers.

findings.title: Zero Automated Test Coverage
findings.description: Zero automated tests exist. Manual validation only in shared QA region. No unit tests, integration tests, regression tests, or CI pipeline.
findings.gap: No automated testing of any kind. No CI pipeline.
findings.recommendation: Implement automated tests starting with core payroll calculation logic.

findings.title: No Encryption at Rest
findings.description: No encryption at rest is configured. Employee data including SSNs and bank account numbers is stored in DB2 tables and sequential files with no encryption.
findings.gap: No KMS, no encryption configuration for sensitive PII data.
findings.recommendation: Enable DB2 native encryption for PII tables. Encrypt output files at rest on EC2 gateway.

findings.title: No Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment exists. Changes validated in a shared QA region only, which lacks production data shapes.
findings.gap: No dedicated staging/sandbox. Shared QA region with no production-equivalent data.
findings.recommendation: Create an isolated staging environment with representative anonymized data.

findings.title: No Compensation or Rollback
findings.description: No compensation or rollback mechanism exists for the payroll batch process. If the job fails mid-run, there is no mechanism to identify which records were processed, roll back partial output, or resume from the failure point.
findings.gap: No saga pattern, no compensating transactions, no checkpoint/restart capability, no idempotency controls.
findings.recommendation: Implement checkpoint/restart with compensation logic. Add record-level tracking to identify partial runs.

findings.title: No Circuit Breakers or Resilience
findings.description: No circuit breakers, retry logic, or timeout configurations exist for external dependency calls. The FTP step has no timeout, no retry on failure, and no fallback behavior.
findings.gap: No resilience patterns for external calls. Single point of failure on FTP connection to EC2 gateway.
findings.recommendation: Add JCL condition codes with retry logic for the FTP step. Implement timeout configuration and fallback.

findings.title: No Queryable Current State
findings.description: The application does not expose its state in any queryable form. No API to check payroll run status or inspect state of a run in progress.
findings.gap: No queryable state endpoints. State locked inside DB2 tables and sequential files.
findings.recommendation: Build read APIs exposing payroll run status and results.

findings.title: No Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, Smithy model, or any machine-readable API specification exists in the repository.
findings.gap: No machine-readable specification for agent tool generation.
findings.recommendation: Create an openapi.yaml documenting the pricing endpoint: query parameters, response schema, and error cases.

findings.title: No Structured Error Responses
findings.description: All responses are HTTP 200 with HTML. Unknown SKU returns $0.00 with no error indication. No structured error codes, no retryable/terminal categorization.
findings.gap: No error codes, no distinction between success and failure, no structured error body.
findings.recommendation: Implement HTTP status codes (404, 400) and structured JSON error responses with error_code, message, and retryable fields.

findings.title: No Scoped Permissions Model
findings.description: No authorization model exists. Since there is no authentication, there is no mechanism to scope permissions. All callers have identical, unrestricted access to all pricing data.
findings.gap: No permission scoping mechanism — cannot differentiate agent access levels.
findings.recommendation: After implementing authentication (AUTH-Q1), define tiered access via API Gateway usage plans.

findings.title: No Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. No RBAC, ABAC, or method-level controls at any layer.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict actions per caller identity.
findings.recommendation: Implement method-level auth at API Gateway (reject non-GET methods). Plan for future write controls.

findings.title: No Input Validation — Buffer Overflow Risk
findings.description: Zero input validation. parse_query uses strcpy without bounds checking — SKU parameter can overflow 64-byte buffer. qty parsed with atoi (no range validation). Buffer overflow vulnerabilities confirmed in README.
findings.gap: No input validation at any layer. Malformed input accepted without validation or structured rejection.
findings.recommendation: Deploy API Gateway with request validation (SKU: max 64 chars alphanumeric, qty: positive integer 1-10000). Long-term: rewrite with safe string handling.

findings.title: No Schema Versioning or API Contracts
findings.description: No schema versioning, no API versioning, no contract testing. The endpoint URL has no version prefix. No changelog, no breaking change detection.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy. Agent tool bindings would break silently on any change.
findings.recommendation: Version the API (e.g., /v1/pricing) and document the response contract. Add changelog.

findings.title: IaC Without Review Gates or Drift Detection
findings.description: Kubernetes manifests in k8s/ define the deployment infrastructure as code. However, no peer review enforcement, no drift detection, no automated plan review. Manifests manually applied via kubectl.
findings.gap: IaC exists but lacks peer review gates and drift reconciliation.
findings.recommendation: Adopt GitOps (ArgoCD or Flux) to enforce PR review and drift reconciliation.

findings.title: No CI/CD Pipeline
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. Makefile defines install target as manual SCP. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild. No contract testing.
findings.gap: No automated build, test, or contract validation before deployment.
findings.recommendation: Create CI pipeline (GitHub Actions or CodeBuild) with Docker build, smoke test, and ECR push.

findings.title: Manual Rollback Only
findings.description: Kubernetes Deployment supports manual rollback via kubectl rollout undo. No automated rollback triggers, no canary deployment, no traffic shifting.
findings.gap: No automated rollback on failure. Manual operator intervention required.
findings.recommendation: Add Flagger or equivalent for metrics-based automated rollback.

findings.title: No Sandbox/Staging Environment
findings.description: No sandbox or staging environment configuration. Dockerfile enables local container builds but no staging environment definition, no seed data, no environment separation.
findings.gap: No production-equivalent staging environment for agent testing.
findings.recommendation: Create staging namespace with test pricing rules and Kustomize overlays for environment separation.

findings.title: No Distributed Tracing or Structured Logging
findings.description: No distributed tracing (no X-Ray, no OpenTelemetry). No structured logging — CGI binary produces no logs. Apache produces unstructured access logs. No correlation IDs.
findings.gap: Cannot trace agent-initiated requests through the system.
findings.recommendation: Deploy Envoy or OTEL collector sidecar for request traces and structured JSON logs.

findings.title: No Alerting on Error Rates or Latency
findings.description: No alerting configuration. No CloudWatch alarms, no Prometheus rules. Kubernetes probes provide health but no alerting thresholds.
findings.gap: Service degradation affecting agents would go undetected.
findings.recommendation: Deploy Prometheus with alerting rules or CloudWatch Container Insights with alarms.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting Configured
findings.description: No rate limiting is configured at any layer. No API Gateway throttling, no WAF rules, no Ingress rate annotations, no application-level rate limiting. A runaway agent loop could send unlimited requests.
findings.gap: No rate limiting at the API layer. Agent traffic storms could overwhelm the service.
findings.recommendation: Add an Ingress resource with rate-limiting annotations, or deploy an API Gateway with throttling configuration.

findings.title: Machine-Readable API Specification
findings.description: No OpenAPI, Swagger, AsyncAPI, GraphQL schema, or equivalent machine-readable specification exists in the repository.
findings.gap: Agent tool generation requires manual authoring that will drift from actual behavior.
findings.recommendation: Create an OpenAPI 3.0 specification documenting both endpoints (GET /rates and POST /quote) with request/response schemas.

findings.title: Structured Error Responses
findings.description: Error responses are minimal ({ error: 'string' }) with HTTP status codes. No error code taxonomy, no retryable indicator, no structured error format.
findings.gap: Agents cannot distinguish retriable from terminal errors.
findings.recommendation: Implement structured error format: { error_code, message, retryable }. Map database errors to retriable and validation errors to non-retriable.

findings.title: Scoped Permissions (Least Privilege)
findings.description: The application has a single API key that grants full access to all endpoints. No mechanism to differentiate access levels — all callers get identical permissions.
findings.gap: No scoped permission model. Cannot grant read-only access to /rates without also granting access to /quote.
findings.recommendation: Introduce API Gateway with usage plans and per-consumer API keys, or implement Cognito with OAuth scopes mapped to endpoint access.

findings.title: Action-Level Authorization
findings.description: No action-level authorization exists. The middleware only validates a single shared API key. No RBAC, ABAC, or permission differentiation between GET and POST operations.
findings.gap: Cannot restrict an agent to read-only operations while blocking computation operations within the same authentication context.
findings.recommendation: Implement method-level authorization at API Gateway or within application middleware.

findings.title: Credential Management
findings.description: API key is hardcoded in source code (server.js line 9). MongoDB connection string with IP address is also hardcoded (line 12). K8s deployment references a Kubernetes secret, but application source still embeds credentials.
findings.gap: Credentials embedded in source code. No secrets management system. No rotation capability.
findings.recommendation: Remove hardcoded credentials. Read from environment variables. Integrate AWS Secrets Manager for credential storage and rotation.

findings.title: Immutable Audit Logging

findings.title: No Circuit Breakers or Resilience Patterns
findings.description: Synchronous SOAP call to external payment gateway with no circuit breaker, no timeout, no retry logic, and no error handling.

findings.title: No Rate Limiting or Throttling
findings.description: No rate limiting at any layer. No API Gateway, no WAF, no application-level rate limiting middleware.
findings.gap: No rate limiting to prevent agent loops from overwhelming the application.

findings.title: State Not Queryable in Structured Form
findings.description: Show and index actions exist but render HTML only. An agent cannot programmatically query current state.

portfolio_level_findings.title: Centralized Identity Plane
portfolio_level_findings.finding: No shared identity provider detected across any repository. All 11 services lack machine identity authentication (AUTH-Q1 is BLOCKER in all 11). No Cognito, Okta, or shared auth middleware found.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: AUTH-Q1 is BLOCKER in all 11 repositories. No shared identity provider configuration found in any report.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Deploy a centralized identity provider (Amazon Cognito with app client credentials) that all services can use for agent M2M authentication.
portfolio_level_findings.contextual_annotations: This finding directly relates to the cross-cutting BLOCKER AUTH-Q1. Resolving PORT-ARA-Q1 resolves AUTH-Q1 for all services simultaneously.

portfolio_level_findings.title: Cross-Service Audit Correlation
portfolio_level_findings.finding: No shared audit correlation mechanism detected. AUTH-Q6 (immutable audit logging) is RISK-SAFETY in 10 services. No shared CloudTrail, no consistent trace ID headers, no centralized log aggregation.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: 10 of 11 services have AUTH-Q6 as RISK-SAFETY. No shared trace ID or centralized logging configuration found.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Deploy centralized CloudWatch Logs with consistent trace ID propagation (X-Amzn-Trace-Id) across all services.

portfolio_level_findings.title: Portfolio-Level Rate Limiting
portfolio_level_findings.finding: No shared API gateway or WAF protecting the portfolio perimeter. STATE-Q5 (rate limiting) is RISK-SAFETY in 8 services. Each service lacks individual rate limiting with no portfolio-level protection.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: 8 of 11 services have STATE-Q5 as RISK-SAFETY finding. No shared WAF or API Gateway detected.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Deploy a shared API Gateway or WAF WebACL with portfolio-level rate limiting rules protecting all agent-facing services.

portfolio_level_findings.title: Transitive Dependency Safety
portfolio_level_findings.finding: No dependency information was explicitly provided. Dependencies were not inferrable from individual reports as services appear to be independent legacy applications. No sync dependency chains detected that would create transitive safety risks.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: No dependency_overrides provided. Individual reports show no inter-service references.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Document service dependencies if they exist. Current portfolio appears to consist of independent legacy services.

portfolio_level_findings.title: Agent Identity Governance
portfolio_level_findings.finding: No centralized mechanism to suspend or revoke agent identities across services. AUTH-Q7 (identity suspension) is RISK-SAFETY in 9 services. Each service would need independent agent identity management with no kill switch.
portfolio_level_findings.evidence: 9 of 11 services have AUTH-Q7 as RISK-SAFETY. No centralized identity registry detected.
portfolio_level_findings.recommendation: Deploy centralized agent identity registry (Cognito User Pool with app clients) enabling portfolio-wide suspension of agent identities.
portfolio_level_findings.contextual_annotations: Relates to cross-cutting RISK-SAFETY AUTH-Q7 and PORT-ARA-Q1.
